temperature, different time: thickness decides how long the heat takes to reach the middle. Size Air fryer Oven Thin, about ¾ inch (2 cm) 400°F / 205°C · 7 min 425°F / 220°C · 9 min Standard, about 1 inch (2.5 cm) 400°F / 205°C · 10 min 425°F / 220°C · 13 min Thick, about 1½ inches (4 cm) 400°F / 205°C · 14 min 425°F / 220°C · 18 min The grey-band problem An air fryer does not sear the way a cast-iron pan does. Hot air carries far less heat than metal, so a wet steak spends its first minutes drying, and by the time the surface browns, heat has crept inwards and left a thick band of grey, overcooked meat under a pale crust. The fix is to make the surface brown faster. Pat the steak completely dry, salt it well ahead of time so the surface dries further, preheat the basket fully, and use the highest setting your unit has. Cook one or two steaks at a time with space around them. The result will not match a smoking-hot pan, but it gets close, with much less mess. Worked example A 1-inch ribeye, salted an hour ahead and patted dry. Preheat the air fryer for 4 minutes, cook at 400°F and turn it at 5 minutes; at 10 minutes it should read about 130°F for medium-rare. A thin ¾-inch steak needs about 7 minutes, a thick 1½-inch cut about 14. Rest it for five minutes before cutting. Doneness by temperature Use an instant-read thermometer from the side into the centre. Rare is about 120–125°F, medium-rare 130°F (54°C), medium 140°F and well done 155°F and above; the USDA guideline for whole cuts of beef is 145°F followed by a three-minute rest. Take the steak out about five degrees before your target, since the temperature keeps rising as it rests. Cutting into it to check lets the juices run out. Before it goes in Take the steak out of the fridge 30 minutes before cooking so the centre is not cold. Salt it at least 40 minutes ahead, or just before; anything in between leaves the surface wet. Brush with a little high-smoke-point oil rather than butter, which burns. Add butter, garlic or herbs while the steak rests. About 10 minutes at 400°F for a 1-inch steak cooked to medium-rare, turned at 5 minutes. Thin steaks take around 7 minutes, thick ones around 14. What temperature is medium-rare steak? About 130°F (54°C). The USDA guideline for whole cuts is 145°F with a three-minute rest, which is closer to medium. Can you get a crust on steak in an air fryer? A good one, if the surface is completely dry and the basket is fully preheated. It will not quite match a cast-iron sear, but it comes close. Should I rest steak after air frying? Yes, for about five minutes. The juices settle back into the meat and the temperature rises a few degrees to finish cooking. What is the oven equivalent for steak? 425°F for around 13 minutes in a conventional oven, though a pan or grill gives a better crust.
